extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO and counsel handling reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including the grounds for discipline, respondent rights to respond, publication/notice requirements, and the underlying state professional conduct rules cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 allow the USPTO Director to impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state court or disciplinary body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order is mailed to the respondent and provides an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and impose the reciprocal discipline (here, a public reprimand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent was found to have violated the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the USPTO public reprimand is for violating § 10.23(b)(6) when the respondent was publicly reprimanded by the Supreme Court for the State of Oregon. (The Order adopts the state discipline as the basis for the USPTO action.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Oregon Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1 (competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed to a public reprimand for violating Oregon RPC 1.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public reprimand was predicated upon a determination that the respondent 'undertook her client's representation without making sufficient inquiry into the client's condition and objectives,' reflecting a failure of competence/due diligence as charged under RPC 1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oregon Rules of Professional Conduct 1.4(a) and (b) (communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed to a public reprimand for violating Oregon RPC 1.4(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The misconduct included that respondent 'did not have direct oral communication with her client' and 'failed to communicate adequately with the client,' showing failure to keep client reasonably informed and to explain matters to permit client to make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oregon Rules of Professional Conduct 1.7(a) (conflict of interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed to a public reprimand for violating Oregon RPC 1.7(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states respondent 'engaged in concurrent representation of her client and another client involved in a conflict of interest,' demonstrating prohibited concurrent representation without proper consent or safeguards under RPC 1.7(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to act: 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority: 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions provide the Director's authority to impose reciprocal discipline based on state-imposed discipline and to administer the § 11.24 process described in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Deputy General Counsel for Enrollment and Discipline (OED DGC) shall publish the Final Order and shall publish the specified notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication of the Final Order and a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette and posting of disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room (URL provided in the Order) for public reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED DGC shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires dissemination of the notice to relevant state disciplinary bodies, courts of admission, and the public to ensure awareness of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and address requirements per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11 (certificate of service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service stating the Order was mailed via first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the most recent address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service and use of the address on file are required procedural steps; the Certificate of Service documents compliance with mailing requirements for disciplinary notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity and timeframe to respond (forty days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided respondent an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline within forty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be based on one or more reasons enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to respond within the timeframe may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposition of reciprocal discipline, as occurred here.
